units.title: Hepatitis C virus: virology and transmission
units.guide: +ve sense RNA Flaviviridae, Hepaciviridae subfamily; lipoviral particle bound to VLDL/LDL causing steatosis (HAV, HBV, HDV, HEV do not); 9.7 kb coding ~3000 amino acid polyprotein; structural and non-structural genes separated by host signal peptidase; DAA suffixes NS3 -previr, NS5A -asvir, NS5B -buvir; 7 genotypes with genotype 1 commonest worldwide and genotype 3 commonest in India with the worst prognosis and cirrhosis/HCC link; transmission percutaneous, transfusion 1 in 10,00,000, perinatal/breast feeding low single digits, IV drug users 40-90%, sexual negligible, commonest in CKD patients; no post-exposure prophylaxis.

units.title: Hepatitis C: natural history, diagnosis and treatment
units.guide: Incubation ~50 days then acute anicteric hepatitis (usually undiagnosed, variable enzymes, fulminant failure 0.1-1%) → chance for chronic hepatitis → cirrhosis / liver failure / portal hypertension → HCC; serological window with HCV RNA before anti-HCV, waning anti-HCV and seroreversion in clearance; anti-HCV EIA positive means acute/chronic/recovered, negative means no contact except in CKD, haemodialysis or HIV where HCV RNA is needed; fibroscan to rule out cirrhosis; SVR 99.5-99.7% in chronic HCV, 75% in cirrhosis, 60% in decompensated disease; new pangenotypic DAAs with high SVR, treat anyone above 12 years; NS3 glecaprevir/simeprevir, NS5A velpatasvir (not available in India), NS5B sofosbuvir with ribavirin, 12 weeks for chronic HCV with cirrhosis; extrahepatic: Sjogren's, salivary gland marginal zone lymphoma, mixed cryoglobulinaemia type 2/3, porphyria cutanea tarda, lichen planus, MPGN, Hashimoto thyroiditis.
